message.content:
**Uno – Game Rules** *Uno* is a fast‑paced card game that’s easy to learn and fun for all ages. The goal is simple: be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever score you set) by getting rid of all your cards before the others. --- ### 1. Setup | Step | What Happens | Why | |------|--------------|-----| | 1 | **Deal** 7 cards to each player. | Gives everyone a starting hand. | | 2 | Place the remaining deck face‑down as the **draw pile**. | Source of new cards. | | 3 | Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the **discard pile**. | Sets the initial color/number. | | 4 | If the flipped card is a special card (Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Wild, or Wild Draw Four), apply its effect immediately. | Keeps the game fair from the start. | --- ### 2. Turn Order | Direction | How It Works | When It Changes | |-----------|--------------|-----------------| | Clockwise | Players take turns in order around the table. | When a **Reverse** card is played. | | Counter‑clockwise | Same as above but opposite direction. | When a **Reverse** card is played again. | --- ### 3. Playing a Card | Condition | What You Can Do | Why | |-----------|-----------------|-----| | Matching **color** | Play any card of the same color as the top discard. | Keeps the theme consistent. | | Matching **number/symbol** | Play any card with the same number or action symbol. | Allows flexibility. | | **Wild** | Play any time; choose the next color. | Lets you change the game’s direction. | | **Wild Draw Four** | Play only if you have no other playable card. | Adds a strategic twist. | If you can’t play, you must **draw one card** from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. --- ### 4. Special Cards | Card | Effect | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **Skip** | Next player loses their turn. | If two Skips are consecutive, the third player is skipped. | | **Reverse** | Changes the direction of play. | In a 2‑player game, it acts like a Skip. | | **Draw Two (+2)** | Next player draws two cards and loses their turn. | If a +2 is stacked on another +2, the next player draws four. | | **Wild** | Player chooses the next color. | No penalty. | | **Wild Draw Four (+4)** | Player chooses the next color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. | Must be challenged if you suspect the player had a matching color. | --- ### 5. “Uno” Call When you’re down to **one card**, shout “UNO!” before your opponent takes their turn. If you forget: - If the next player notices, they can call you out. - You must then draw **two penalty cards** from the draw pile. If you’re caught after the next player has already taken their turn, you still draw two cards. --- ### 6. Winning a Round | Condition | Scoring | Why | |-----------|---------|-----| | A player discards their last card | They win the round. | Ends the current round. | | **Points** | Add up the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value
• Draw Two, Skip, Reverse = 20 points
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points | Tallies how much the winner earned. | | **Round End** | Winner receives the sum of the opponents’ points. | Rewards the winner. | --- ### 7. Game End | Condition | What Happens | Why | |-----------|--------------|-----| | First player reaches **500 points** (or agreed target) | Game ends; that player is the overall winner. | Sets a clear end goal. | | **Alternative** | Stop after a set number of rounds. | Useful for shorter sessions. | --- ### 8. House Rules & Variations | Variation | How It Works | Why | |-----------|--------------|-----| | **Stacking** | Players can stack +2 or +4 cards on each other instead of drawing. | Adds strategy. | | **Seven‑Zero** | When a player plays a 7, they can swap hands with anyone. When a 0 is played, everyone rotates hands clockwise. | Fun twist. | | **Speed Uno** | No “UNO” call; play as fast as possible. | For adrenaline junkies. | | **Custom Decks** | Use themed decks (e.g., Disney, Pokémon). | Keeps the game fresh. | Feel free to tweak these rules to suit your group’s preferences. Have fun playing Uno!
